Indian Standard
METHODS OF SAMPLING FOR AGRICULTURAL MACHINERY AND EQUIPMENT
PART 1 HAND-TOOLS AND HAND-OPERATED/ANIMALDRAWN ( EQUIPMENT

First Revision )
0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part 1 ) ( First iievision ) wasadopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 1'7 March 1.987, after the draft finalized by the Sampling Methods for Food Products and Agricultural Inputs Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council. 0.2 The original version of this standard was published in 1974 and prescribed lot inspection plans for all types of agricultural machinery and tractors. With the considerable increase in the production of different types of agricultural machinery and equipment, the number of Indian Standards formulated in this field had also increased. It was felt that the original standard might not cater to the needs of all types of agricultural machinery and tractors, as the acceptable quality level desired, cost of equipment, cost and time of testing and number of items usually supplied in a lot, were quite different. 0.3 In this revised version, different types of equipment have ,been classified into two first group covers hand-tools, such as sickles, budding knives, and the second group animal-drawn equipment, such as sprayers, drills. 0.4 Whereas Part 1 covers equipment, power-operated 1. SCOPE agricultural machinery. homogeneous groups. hand-hoes, KHURPIES covers hand-operated ploughs, cultivators and The and and and

hand-tools and animal-drawn/hand-operated equipment will be covered in Part 2.

1.1 This standard ( Part 1 ) prescribes the scale of sampling and criteria of' contjrmity for determining the acceptability or otherwise of handtc,c,is and animal-drawn/hand-operated agricultural machinery and equipment.

13 : 7201 ( Part 1 ) - 1987 2.3.1 These tools/equipments shall be selected at random from the lot guidance can be obtained from IS : 4903-1968*. and for this purpose, sampling may The procedures of simple random samplin g or systematic be followed. 2.3.1.1 Sinzple vandom sampling - In case the lot consisrs cf numbers of tools/equipments, such that each of these itc:rls is easill. ic!entifinble, the method of simple random samplin y sliall be fo!lo~& for selecting According to this method, the sample of the items for the sample. requisite size n shall be dra\vn from a lot of size Kin such a manner that while selecting the items, the chance for any item of the lot being included in the sample should be the same. An item once dra\\-n should not be placed back in the lot. For this purpose, random number tables may be used.
Example:

It is desired to obtain a sample of 8 sickles from a lot of 200 sickles. If the sickles in the lot are mentally assigned serial numbers up to 200, the problem then becomes to.obtain 8 random numbers in the range of 1 to 200. Taking the 3-diqited random numbers from Appendix B of IS : 4905-1968" and starting \\:ith any number say 20, occurring in the 8th row and 11, 12 and 13 columns and proceeding downwards, numerals less than 200 are noted down. Thus the 8 numerals as obtained are 20, 53, 35, 140, 62, 174, 177 and 142. When arranged in ascending order of magnitude, the numerals become 20, 35,53,62, 142, 149, 174 and li7. The items in the lot corresponding to these numbers shall then be selected to. constitute the required random sample of 8 sickles. 2.3.1.2 ,Systematic .rampling -- When the items in a lot are presented in an orderly manner, it should be possible to considerably simplify the selection of random sample of the required size. The method consists item from a lot of .Y items and of first selecting a single sample thereafter selecting items at regular pre-determined intervals to make up the desired sample of size n. For this purpose the integra.1 part of J\:lrz ( say r ) is taken `as the interval and then the items are counted in one order and every sth item thus counted is withdrawn until the sample of required size is obtained.
Example:

Suppose 100 sprayers in a lot are stored in an orderly manner Calculate and a sample of 3 sprayers is to be selected at random. the integral part of 10013 ( = 33.3 ) which is 33. Starting from any sprayer ( random number tables may be used), count the sprayers in

3. NUMBER

OF

AND

CONFORMITY

3.1 The hand-tools/equipments selected according to co1 1 and `2 of Table 1 or Table 2 as the case may be, shall be examined for visual, dimensional \vcight and hardness requirements as given in the relevant material specification. Any tool equipment failing to satisfy one or more of these requirements shall be.considered as defective. The lot shall be considered as conforminS to these requirements if the number of defectivcs found in the sample is less than or equal to the corresponding permissible number of tlefectives given in co1 3 of Table 1 or Table 2 as the case may be. 3.2 The lot having been found satisfactory according to 3.1, shall be further tested for requirements other than those covered in 3.1. For this purpose, the number of tools,`equipments given for sub-sample in co1 4 of Table 1 or Table 2 as the case may be, shall be selected from the lot. These tools,equipments shall be selected from those already The lot shall be examined according to 3.1 and found satisfactory. declared as conforming to the requirements of the relevant material specification if none of the tools/equipments in the sub-sample fails in any of these requirements.
